title: 核对整页排队与并发读取的收益及合并边界
method: Two warmed ScreenReaders; next page arrives100ms after previous read starts. Serial reader retains previous-page caches; parallel reader has its own warmed cache. Measures complete arrangement, excluding capture, UI and engine startup. Local images and raw observations remain local. Third case is a static-frame-cache control, not evidence of queue savings.
parity: No fact differences across three cases in either round, excluding timing/confidence/counter timing. Not an independent accuracy oracle.
rejected: Creating a new thread versus reusing a thread did not increase detector time consistently; no request-lifetime change adopted.
state_merge: Isolated reproduction: independently preparing two timeline snapshots and committing newer then older loses the latest resource. Preparing each completion against the latest timeline preserves it. This is a risk of naive concurrent integration, not a claimed bug in current sequential production.
next: Keep latest-page and historical reads separate, serialize completion reduction against the newest timeline, include in-flight older frames in compaction watermark, and verify pause/reset/close and short-page retention before native capture/UI comparison. Do not simply duplicate the current worker closure.
limits: No production latency improvement shipped in this batch.
Only two page-switch pairs plus a cached control, two rounds; no p95 claim.
CPU cost can increase; memory and game co-running are unmeasured.
Current/history priority and chronological commit remain pending.
